excerpt: What makes Folly Road one of Charleston's most crash-prone corridors, and your options after a collision on James Island.
keyTakeaways: Folly Road is James Island's primary corridor and one of Charleston's most crash-prone roads due to heavy traffic, limited turn lanes, and dense commercial development. Common accidents include rear-end collisions, T-bone crashes at intersections, and pedestrian strikes. Liable parties may include other drivers, the City of Charleston, or SCDOT for road design deficiencies. South Carolina's 3-year statute of limitations applies (S.C. Code 15-3-530), and comparative fault bars recovery at 51% or more.

faqs.question: Why is Folly Road so dangerous for drivers?
faqs.answer: Folly Road is the only route between James Island, downtown Charleston, and Folly Beach, concentrating all traffic onto a single corridor. It combines high-volume commuter traffic with tourist beach traffic, dense commercial driveways, frequent speed limit changes, limited shoulders for cyclists and pedestrians, and regular flooding. During summer months the traffic volume surges dramatically, making rear-end collisions and left-turn crashes especially common.

faqs.question: What should I do after a car accident on Folly Road?
faqs.answer: Move to safety if possible since secondary crashes are a real risk on this busy road. Call 911 for police and medical assistance. Seek medical attention within 24 hours even if symptoms seem minor. Photograph vehicle damage, road conditions, and injuries. Exchange information with the other driver. Identify witnesses. Do not give recorded statements to the other driver's insurance company. Contact a car accident lawyer promptly to preserve traffic camera and surveillance footage.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim after a Folly Road crash?
faqs.answer: South Carolina allows three years from the date of the accident for personal injury claims (S.C. Code section 15-3-530) and three years from the date of death for wrongful death claims. However, critical evidence like traffic camera footage and business surveillance video is typically overwritten within 30-72 hours, so contacting a lawyer within the first few days is essential.

faqs.question: Can I recover damages if I was partially at fault for the accident?
faqs.answer: Yes. South Carolina follows a modified comparative fault rule (Nelson v. Concrete Supply Co.) that allows recovery as long as your fault is less than 51 percent. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault. Insurance companies frequently argue that drivers on Folly Road were following too closely or were distracted, but an attorney can counter these arguments with evidence.

faqs.question: Can I sue a bar on Folly Beach if a drunk driver caused my accident?
faqs.answer: Potentially, yes. Under South Carolina's dram shop law (S.C. Code section 61-2-145), bars and restaurants can be held liable if they serve alcohol to a visibly intoxicated person who then causes a DUI crash. Folly Road is the primary route home from Folly Beach's bars, making dram shop liability a relevant factor in many DUI crashes on this corridor.

faqs.question: What types of injuries are common in Folly Road car accidents?
faqs.answer: Common injuries include traumatic brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, broken bones, internal organ damage, whiplash and soft tissue injuries, and in the most severe cases, wrongful death. T-bone collisions at intersections and high-speed rear-end crashes tend to produce the most severe injuries. Pedestrian and bicycle crashes on Folly Road are also disproportionately severe due to the lack of protected infrastructure.
